answer:
**A hidden activation is a mixture of signals, not necessarily one named concept per neuron.** A neuron may respond to several unrelated-looking features because the network represents more useful directions than it has independent coordinates. Steering modifies activations during inference; a sparse autoencoder tries to describe those activations using a larger set of selectively active features. [1](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2023/monosemantic-features/index.html)

For steering, collect contrasting examples, such as responses with and without a desired style. Estimate a direction v from their activations and intervene with $h'=h+\alpha v$ at a chosen layer. Alpha controls strength. This may change the target behavior, but the direction may also encode correlated properties such as length or sentiment.

An SAE learns a sparse code z that reconstructs the original activation h. The reconstruction term preserves information while a sparsity penalty discourages activating every feature. An overcomplete dictionary can represent several distinct directions that were mixed in individual neuron coordinates.

**Interpretation needs intervention.** If a feature activates on examples labeled “uncertainty,” that correlation alone does not establish that it causally controls calibrated uncertainty. Activate or suppress it, test unseen prompts, and measure unintended changes. Human-readable labels are useful hypotheses, not complete descriptions of what a feature means. Steering and SAEs offer tools for investigating representations, not guaranteed surgical control over a model's beliefs or behavior.

**Technical details and references.**

Activation steering adds a chosen direction to hidden states, often derived from contrasting example sets. It can change behavior without updating weights, but effects depend on layer, strength, prompt, and off-target changes. [1](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2023/monosemantic-features/index.html)

A sparse autoencoder reconstructs activations through an overcomplete sparse code:

$$z=\operatorname{ReLU}(W_ex+b_e),\quad \hat x=W_dz+b_d,\quad L=\|x-\hat x\|^2+\lambda\|z\|_1.$$

Sparsity encourages features that activate selectively, helping separate concepts superposed in neuron coordinates. “Monosemantic” is an interpretive goal, not a guarantee that each feature has one complete human-readable meaning. Validate with interventions and held-out examples; correlated activation labels alone do not establish causal control or exhaustive understanding of the model.
